title: Who Did It? Not With Passive Se

sections.title: Leaving the doer out
sections.content: You know the passive with *ser* from B1 Unit 18: *El puente fue construido por el alcalde*, where *por* names who did it. Passive *se* does the opposite: it is there to leave the doer out. So in normal Spanish it does not take *por* plus the doer. You can say *Se construyó el puente*, or *El puente fue construido por el alcalde*, but not *Se construyó el puente por el alcalde*.

sections.title: What do you want to say?
rows: The doer is unknown or does not matter
You want to name the doer and keep the passive
El puente fue construido por el alcalde.
You want to name the doer and keep it short

items.spanish: Los resultados fueron publicados por la directora.
items.english: The results were published by the director.

sections.content: Watch the other *por*. In *Se compran billetes por internet*, *por* means "over" or "by means of", not "done by", so it is fine. The test is simple: if the word after *por* is the person or group who did the action, use *ser* or an active sentence instead of *se*.
